subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has cellular level of organisation?
explain: Porifera shows cellular level of organisation; cells not organised into tissues.

subject: Biology
prompt: Flame cells are excretory structures in which phylum?
explain: Flame cells (protonephridia) are the excretory organs in Platyhelminthes.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which animal is called the 'connecting link' between Annelida & Arthropoda?
explain: Peripatus (Onychophora) shares features of both Annelida and Arthropoda.

subject: Biology
prompt: Open circulatory system is found in which phylum?
explain: Arthropoda has open circulatory system; blood flows in haemocoel, not closed vessels.

subject: Biology
prompt: Water vascular system is characteristic of which phylum?
explain: Water vascular system (ambulacral system) is unique to phylum Echinodermata.

subject: Biology
prompt: Radial symmetry in adult but bilateral symmetry in larva is seen in:
explain: Echinoderms show radial symmetry as adults but bilateral symmetry in larval stage.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Arthropoda has book lungs as respiratory organ?
explain: Arachnids (spiders, scorpions) respire through book lungs.

subject: Biology
prompt: Notochord is present in which larval stage of Urochordata?
explain: In Urochordata (tunicates), notochord is present only in the tail of tadpole larva.

subject: Biology
prompt: Organ of Jacobson (vomeronasal organ) is present in:
explain: Jacobson's organ (vomeronasal organ) is well-developed in reptiles for chemoreception.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which feature distinguishes Aves from all other vertebrates?
explain: Feathers are unique to Aves; no other vertebrate class possesses them.

subject: Biology
prompt: Coelom derived from mesoderm by schizocoely is called:
explain: Schizocoelom forms by splitting of mesodermal bands; seen in annelids, arthropods, molluscs.

subject: Biology
prompt: Nematocysts (cnidoblasts) are present in which phylum?
explain: Cnidoblasts bearing nematocysts are the stinging cells unique to Coelenterata (Cnidaria).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has pseudocoelom (body cavity not lined by mesoderm)?
explain: Aschelminthes (Nematoda) are pseudocoelomates; body cavity not fully lined by mesoderm.

subject: Biology
prompt: Lateral line system (sense organ) is found in:
explain: Lateral line system detects water currents and is present in fish (Pisces).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which mammal lays eggs (oviparous mammal)?
explain: Platypus (Ornithorhynchus) belongs to Prototheria and is an egg-laying mammal.

subject: Biology
prompt: Malpighian tubules are excretory organs in:
explain: Malpighian tubules are the excretory structures in insects (class Insecta, phylum Arthropoda).

subject: Biology
prompt: Green glands (antennal glands) function as excretory organs in:
explain: Green glands (antennal glands) are excretory organs in crustaceans like Prawn.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which amphibian is viviparous?
explain: Salamandra (fire salamander) is viviparous among amphibians, gives birth to live young.

subject: Biology
prompt: Balanoglossus belongs to which phylum?
explain: Balanoglossus (tongue worm) is a classic example of phylum Hemichordata.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom?
explain: Arthropoda is the largest phylum with maximum number of species in the animal kingdom.

subject: Biology
prompt: Spongocoel & ostia are structures found in which phylum?
explain: Spongocoel (central cavity) and ostia (pores) are characteristic structures of sponges (Porifera).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Reptilia includes crocodiles?
explain: Crocodiles belong to order Crocodilia under class Reptilia.

subject: Biology
prompt: Coelenterata show which type of body plan?
explain: Coelenterata have tissue level of organisation; cells form tissues but no organs.

subject: Biology
prompt: Pneumatic bones (hollow bones) are an adaptation in:
explain: Birds (Aves) have hollow (pneumatic) bones to reduce body weight for flight.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is a cold-blooded (poikilothermic) vertebrate?
explain: Fishes are poikilothermic (ectothermic); body temperature varies with environment.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum shows tissue level of organisation?
explain: Coelenterata (Cnidaria) shows tissue level; cells performing same function are arranged into tissues.

subject: Biology
prompt: Hermaphroditic (bisexual) animals include which phylum?
explain: Platyhelminthes (tapeworms, planaria) are hermaphrodites; both male & female organs in same individual.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has organ-system level of organisation first?
explain: Platyhelminthes is the first phylum to show true organ-system level of body organisation.

subject: Biology
prompt: Bilateral symmetry first appears in which phylum?
explain: Platyhelminthes is the first phylum to show bilateral symmetry in the animal kingdom.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum is exclusively marine & triploblastic coelomate?
explain: Echinoderms are exclusively marine, triploblastic, coelomate animals with water vascular system.

subject: Biology
prompt: Book gills are respiratory organs in which arthropod?
explain: Limulus (king crab) possesses book gills for respiration; book lungs are in arachnids like scorpion.

subject: Biology
prompt: Notochord is present throughout life in which chordate?
explain: In Cephalochordata (e.g. Amphioxus/Branchiostoma) notochord persists from head to tail throughout life.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is the correct example of class Chondrichthyes?
explain: Scoliodon is a cartilaginous fish (Chondrichthyes); Rohu, Labeo, Catla are bony fishes (Osteichthyes).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which mammal has a cloaca (common opening)?
explain: Prototheria (monotremes) like Echidna & Platypus have a cloaca, like reptiles & birds.

subject: Biology
prompt: Tympanic membrane (eardrum) first appears in which vertebrate class?
explain: Tympanic membrane first appears in Amphibia for hearing airborne sound waves.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has a true coelom formed by enterocoely?
explain: Echinoderms form coelom by enterocoely (outpouching of archenteron); they are deuterostomes.

subject: Biology
prompt: Suckers & hooks for attachment are found in which parasite?
explain: Taenia (tapeworm, Platyhelminthes) has scolex with suckers & hooks for attachment to host intestine.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Mammalia gives birth to poorly developed young (pouch)?
explain: Metatheria (marsupials) e.g. Kangaroo, bear young in marsupium (pouch) for further development.

subject: Biology
prompt: Typhlosole increases absorptive surface in which animal?
explain: Typhlosole is a dorsal fold of intestine in earthworm (Pheretima) that increases absorption area.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is a correct example of phylum Mollusca?
explain: Chiton is a mollusc; Nereis is Annelida; Ophiura is Echinodermata; Limulus is Arthropoda.

subject: Biology
prompt: Radula (rasping organ for feeding) is present in which phylum?
explain: Radula is a file-like feeding organ found in most Mollusca (except bivalves) for scraping food.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which reptile has a 4-chambered heart?
explain: Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a complete 4-chambered heart; others have 3-chambered.

subject: Biology
prompt: Pearl is secreted by which layer of Mollusca shell?
explain: Nacreous (inner) layer of molluscan shell secretes nacre (mother of pearl); pearl forms around irritant.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has nephridia as excretory organs?
explain: Annelida (earthworm, Nereis) use nephridia for osmoregulation and excretion of nitrogenous wastes.

subject: Biology
prompt: Parapodia used for locomotion are found in which annelid?
explain: Nereis (polychaete) has parapodia (lateral appendages) used for locomotion; absent in earthworm & leech.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has a true coelom & shows metameric segmentation?
explain: Annelida are triploblastic, true coelomates showing metameric segmentation (e.g., Earthworm).

subject: Biology
prompt: Chitinous exoskeleton is a characteristic feature of which phylum?
explain: Arthropoda have a hard chitinous exoskeleton that must be shed (moulted) for growth.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Mammalia is characterised by presence of a placenta?
explain: Eutheria (placental mammals) nourish young via placenta; e.g., humans, whales, bats.

subject: Biology
prompt: Closed circulatory system first appears in which phylum?
explain: Annelida are the first to possess a true closed circulatory system with blood vessels.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which animal is the correct example of class Osteichthyes?
explain: Labeo (rohu) is a bony fish (Osteichthyes); Scoliodon, Torpedo, Pristis are Chondrichthyes.

subject: Biology
prompt: Dorsal hollow nerve cord is a chordate character; invertebrate nerve cord is:
explain: Non-chordates (invertebrates) have a ventral solid nerve cord, unlike the dorsal hollow one in chordates.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has organisms with a mantle that secretes the shell?
explain: In Mollusca, the mantle (fold of body wall) secretes the calcareous shell.

subject: Biology
prompt: Gizzard (muscular stomach for grinding food) is found in which animal?
explain: Earthworm (Pheretima) has a muscular gizzard for grinding food particles.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is the correct example of class Cyclostomata?
explain: Petromyzon (lamprey) and Myxine (hagfish) are jawless vertebrates of class Cyclostomata.

subject: Biology
prompt: Tube feet (podia) in Echinoderms are used for:
explain: Tube feet connected to the water vascular system help echinoderms in locomotion and capturing food.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which arthropod class includes insects with 3 pairs of legs?
explain: Class Insecta (Hexapoda) is defined by 3 pairs of jointed legs and a body divided into head, thorax, abdomen.

subject: Biology
prompt: Metagenesis (alternation of sexual & asexual generations) occurs in:
explain: Cnidaria (e.g., Obelia) show metagenesis: asexual polyp stage alternates with sexual medusa stage.

subject: Biology
prompt: Air bladder (swim bladder) to regulate buoyancy is present in:
explain: Bony fishes (Osteichthyes) have an air bladder that regulates buoyancy; absent in cartilaginous fishes.

subject: Biology
prompt: Ovoviviparous reproduction is seen in which example?
explain: Scoliodon is ovoviviparous: eggs are retained inside the body until hatching, then young are born alive.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Amphibia includes Salamanders & Newts?
explain: Urodela (=Caudata) includes tailed amphibians like salamanders and newts (e.g., Ambystoma).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which Cnidarian exists only as a polyp (no medusa stage)?
explain: Hydra exists only as a polyp; Aurelia is only medusa; Obelia shows both polyp and medusa stages.

subject: Biology
prompt: Setae (chitinous bristles) for locomotion are present in:
explain: Earthworm uses chitinous setae embedded in the body wall for locomotion and burrowing.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is a correct example of a colonial Cnidarian (siphonophore)?
explain: Physalia is a colonial siphonophore (Cnidaria) where individuals are polymorphic and interdependent.

subject: Biology
prompt: Post-anal tail is a chordate feature. It is absent/reduced in which adult?
explain: Adult frogs reabsorb their tail during metamorphosis; the post-anal tail is lost in adult anurans.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has organisms called 'sea walnut' or 'comb jellies'?
explain: Ctenophora (comb jellies, e.g., Pleurobrachia) are marine, bioluminescent, with comb plates for locomotion.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which vertebrate class has 2-chambered heart (1 auricle + 1 ventricle)?
explain: Fishes have a 2-chambered heart; Amphibia & most Reptilia have 3 chambers; Aves & Mammalia have 4.

subject: Biology
prompt: Asymmetry (no symmetry) is characteristic of which animal group?
explain: Most adult sponges (Porifera) are asymmetrical; no definite plane divides them into equal halves.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Reptilia includes lizards and snakes?
explain: Squamata includes lizards and snakes; Chelonia = turtles; Crocodilia = crocodiles; Rhynchocephalia = Sphenodon.

subject: Biology
prompt: Nephridia in earthworm & malpighian tubules in insects both function as:
explain: Both nephridia (Annelida) and Malpighian tubules (Arthropoda/Insecta) are excretory structures removing nitrogenous waste.

subject: Biology
prompt: Collar cells (choanocytes) line the spongocoel of which phylum?
explain: Choanocytes are flagellated collar cells unique to Porifera; they create water current & aid in digestion.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which vertebrate has a 3-chambered heart (2 auricles + 1 ventricle)?
explain: Amphibians have 3-chambered heart; exception: crocodiles (Reptilia) have 4-chambered heart.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum is characterised by jointed appendages & open circulatory system?
explain: Jointed appendages (arthropoda = jointed legs) and haemocoel-based open circulation define Arthropoda.

subject: Biology
prompt: Cephalisation (head formation) first appears prominently in which phylum?
explain: Platyhelminthes are the first bilaterally symmetrical animals showing distinct head (cephalisation).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which class of Chondrichthyes lacks an operculum covering the gills?
explain: Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish like sharks) have exposed gill slits without an operculum.

subject: Biology
prompt: Organ of Corti (hearing receptor) is located in which structure?
explain: Organ of Corti in the cochlea of the inner ear is the actual receptor for sound (hearing).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum shows polymorphism (different zooids with different functions)?
explain: Colonial Coelenterates (e.g., Physalia) show polymorphism with specialised zooids like gastrozooids, gonozooids.

subject: Biology
prompt: Clitellum is present in which animal and helps in cocoon formation?
explain: Clitellum is a glandular band in earthworm (Pheretima) that secretes cocoon for egg deposition.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is the correct example of class Hirudinea (leeches)?
explain: Hirudinaria (cattle leech) is the classic NCERT example of class Hirudinea under phylum Annelida.

subject: Biology
prompt: Diploblastic body wall (ectoderm + endoderm) with mesoglea is seen in:
explain: Coelenterates are diploblastic; mesoglea (non-cellular jelly) lies between ectoderm and endoderm.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which phylum has animals with a true coelom and unsegmented body?
explain: Mollusca are coelomate (true coelom) but unsegmented, unlike Annelida which are segmented coelomates.

subject: Biology
prompt: Nauplius is the free-swimming larva of which class of Arthropoda?
explain: Nauplius larva is characteristic of Crustacea (e.g., prawn, shrimp, barnacle) — a key NCERT fact.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is a correct example of a jawless vertebrate (Cyclostomata)?
explain: Myxine (hagfish) and Petromyzon (lamprey) are NCERT examples of jawless Cyclostomata.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which feature is unique to mammals among all vertebrates?
explain: Mammary glands (milk-producing) are the defining feature of class Mammalia per NCERT.

subject: Biology
prompt: Trochophore larva is common to which two phyla?
explain: Trochophore larva is shared by Annelida and Mollusca, indicating their evolutionary relationship.

subject: Biology
prompt: Pharyngeal gill slits are present at some stage in ALL members of which group?
explain: Pharyngeal gill slits during development are a universal chordate character (one of 4 basic features).

subject: Biology
prompt: Which mammal has electric organs & is called duck-billed platypus?
explain: Ornithorhynchus (platypus) is a monotreme mammal; has bill, lays eggs & has electric sensory organs.

subject: Biology
prompt: Aristotle's lantern is the jaw apparatus of which Echinoderm class?
explain: Sea urchins (Echinoidea) possess Aristotle's lantern — a complex chewing apparatus of 5 teeth.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which vertebrate class has a 3-chambered heart with an INCOMPLETELY divided ventricle?
explain: Reptiles have 3-chambered heart with incompletely divided ventricle (except crocodiles which have 4-chambered heart).

subject: Biology
prompt: Canal system is characteristic of which phylum?
explain: Porifera possess an elaborate canal system (asconoid, syconoid, leuconoid) for circulation of water through their body.

subject: Biology
prompt: Scales absent; moist skin used for respiration—this describes which class?
explain: Amphibians lack scales and have moist, glandular skin that supplements lung/gill respiration (cutaneous respiration).
